title: 2 Samuel Chapter 12 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Samuel chapter 12 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 12 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Samuel Chapter 12.

questions.question: Who did the LORD send to David in 2 Samuel 12?
options: Nathan
Samuel
Elijah
Gad
questions.correctAnswer: Nathan
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12:1 states that the LORD sent Nathan unto David.

questions.question: In Nathan's story to David, what was the condition of the poor man's lamb?
options: It was the only lamb he had and was like a daughter to him
It was one among many sheep
It was wild and untamed
It was meant for sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: It was the only lamb he had and was like a daughter to him
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12:3 describes the poor man's lamb as the only one he had and it was unto him as a daughter.

questions.question: What did the rich man do when a traveller came to him?
options: He took from his own flock to prepare food
He took the poor man's lamb to prepare food
He sent the traveller away without food
He gave the traveller money to buy food
questions.correctAnswer: He took the poor man's lamb to prepare food
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12:4 states that the rich man spared to take from his own flock but took the poor man's lamb to dress for the traveller.

questions.question: How did David react to the story Nathan told him?
options: David was angry and said the man deserved to die
David ignored the story
David laughed at the story
David was confused about the story
questions.correctAnswer: David was angry and said the man deserved to die
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12:5 shows David's anger was greatly kindled and he said the man who did this shall surely die.

questions.question: What punishment did David say the man should receive for his actions?
options: He should restore the lamb fourfold
He should be forgiven
He should be banished from the city
He should pay a small fine
questions.correctAnswer: He should restore the lamb fourfold
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12:6 says David declared the man shall restore the lamb fourfold because he had no pity.

questions.question: What was Nathan's response to David after David pronounced judgment on the rich man?
options: Nathan said, 'Thou art the man.'
Nathan agreed with David's judgment without comment
Nathan asked David to forgive the man
Nathan left without saying anything
questions.correctAnswer: Nathan said, 'Thou art the man.'
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12:7 records Nathan saying to David, 'Thou art the man.'

questions.question: According to Nathan, what had the LORD given David before this sin?
options: His master's house, wives, and the house of Israel and Judah
Only a small kingdom
No possessions or power
A large army only
questions.correctAnswer: His master's house, wives, and the house of Israel and Judah
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12:8 states that God gave David his master's house, wives, and the house of Israel and Judah.

questions.question: What commandment did David despise according to Nathan?
options: The commandment of the LORD not to do evil in His sight
The commandment to build the temple
The commandment to not go to war
The commandment to fast and pray
questions.correctAnswer: The commandment of the LORD not to do evil in His sight
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12:9 explains David despised the commandment of the LORD to not do evil in His sight.

questions.question: What consequence did the LORD declare would never depart from David's house?
options: The sword
A famine
A plague
Poverty
questions.correctAnswer: The sword
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12:10 states that the sword shall never depart from David's house.

questions.question: What did the LORD say He would raise up against David out of his own house?
options: Evil
Peace
Wealth
A great army
questions.correctAnswer: Evil
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12:11 states the LORD will raise up evil against David out of his own house.

questions.question: True or False: Nathan told David that his sin was done in secret but would be revealed publicly.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12:12 says David did it secretly but God will do it before all Israel and the sun.

questions.question: True or False: David declared that the man who took the poor man's lamb should be forgiven and spared.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: David declared in 2 Samuel 12:5 that the man who did this should surely die, showing no forgiveness.

questions.question: True or False: Nathan was sent to David by the LORD to confront him about his sin.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12:1 states the LORD sent Nathan to David to deliver the message.

questions.question: True or False: Nathan spared David from any punishment after confessing his sin.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Though Nathan said the LORD put away David's sin and he should not die (2 Samuel 12:13), punishment through consequences and evil from his own house was declared in earlier verses.

questions.question: In 2 Samuel 12, which event comes first?
options: David's anger against the man who took the lamb
Nathan telling David he is the man
The LORD sending Nathan to David
David confessing his sin
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD sending Nathan to David
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12:1 shows the LORD first sent Nathan to David before any other events.

medium.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 12 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Samuel Chapter 12 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Nathan reveal to David about the nature of his sin according to 2 Samuel 12?
options: David had acted secretly but God would expose it publicly
David had openly confessed his sin to all Israel
David's sin was forgiven without any consequence
David was innocent of the accusations
questions.correctAnswer: David had acted secretly but God would expose it publicly
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12:12 states that David did it secretly, but God would do this thing before all Israel and the sun, revealing his sin publicly.

questions.question: How did David respond when Nathan confronted him with his sin?
options: He confessed and said, 'I have sinned against the LORD.'
He denied the accusation
He became angry and rejected Nathan
He fled from Nathan's presence
questions.correctAnswer: He confessed and said, 'I have sinned against the LORD.'
questions.explanation: In 2 Samuel 12:13, David admits his sin to Nathan by saying, 'I have sinned against the LORD.'

questions.question: What consequence did Nathan say would result from David's sin, despite God putting away his sin?
options: The child born to David would surely die
David would lose his kingdom immediately
David would be struck by a plague
David would be exiled from Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The child born to David would surely die
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12:14 explains that although God put away David's sin, the child born to him would surely die as a consequence.

questions.question: What actions did David take when his child became very sick?
options: He fasted and lay all night upon the earth
He ignored the child's sickness
He sent for other healers besides God
He celebrated with feasts
questions.correctAnswer: He fasted and lay all night upon the earth
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12:16 describes that David fasted and lay all night on the ground, praying for his child's recovery.

questions.question: What was David’s behavior when the elders of his house tried to raise him from the earth?
options: He refused to be raised and did not eat bread with them
He immediately got up and joined them for food
He angrily sent them away
He requested they bring Nathan the prophet
questions.correctAnswer: He refused to be raised and did not eat bread with them
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12:17 states that David would not be raised nor did he eat bread with the elders who came to him.

questions.question: Why did David's servants hesitate to tell him that the child had died?
options: They feared David would vex himself because he was not listening while the child was alive
They wanted to surprise him with good news
They believed the child was still alive
They thought David was indifferent to the child
questions.correctAnswer: They feared David would vex himself because he was not listening while the child was alive
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12:18 explains the servants feared telling David because while the child was alive, he would not listen, so they thought he would be greatly upset if told the child had died.

questions.question: What did David do after he learned that his child was dead?
options: He arose, washed, anointed himself, changed his apparel, worshipped, and then ate
He continued to fast and weep without eating
He went into isolation and refused to pray
He sent for Nathan to rebuke him again
questions.correctAnswer: He arose, washed, anointed himself, changed his apparel, worshipped, and then ate
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12:20 records David's response to the child's death, showing his acceptance by preparing himself and worshipping before eating.

questions.question: How did David explain to his servants his change in behavior after the child's death?
options: He fasted and wept while the child was alive, hoping God might be gracious, but now that the child was dead, he could not bring him back
He said he was no longer sad because he had lost faith
He declared the child's death was a punishment for others
He said the servants misunderstood his feelings
questions.correctAnswer: He fasted and wept while the child was alive, hoping God might be gracious, but now that the child was dead, he could not bring him back
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12:22-23 show David's reasoning that fasting was to seek God's grace for the child's life, but after death, fasting would not change the situation.

questions.question: What biblical virtue does David’s behavior in verses 16-23 most clearly demonstrate?
options: Faith and trust in God despite suffering
Rebellion against God’s will
Self-pity and despair
Ignoring God’s commands
questions.correctAnswer: Faith and trust in God despite suffering
questions.explanation: David’s fasting, prayer, worship, and acceptance of the child’s death illustrate faith and trust in God amidst grief (2 Samuel 12:16-23).

questions.question: Based on 2 Samuel 12, what can a believer learn about approaching God in times of personal crisis?
options: Seek God earnestly through prayer and fasting, but accept His sovereign will
Avoid God and ignore problems
Blame others for personal failures
Demand immediate answers from God
questions.correctAnswer: Seek God earnestly through prayer and fasting, but accept His sovereign will
questions.explanation: David’s example of earnest prayer and fasting combined with acceptance of God’s will (2 Samuel 12:16-23) teaches believers how to approach crises.

questions.question: What does 2 Samuel 12:14 say will happen if one’s sin causes the enemies of the LORD to blaspheme?
options: The child born as a result of the sin shall surely die
The sinner will be immediately forgiven
The enemies will be punished
The sinner’s house will prosper
questions.correctAnswer: The child born as a result of the sin shall surely die
questions.explanation: Verse 14 warns that sin causing blasphemy against God results in the death of the child born to the sinner, emphasizing consequences.

questions.question: True or False: Nathan told David that he would not die because the LORD had put away his sin.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12:13 records Nathan telling David that the LORD had put away his sin and that he would not die.

questions.question: True or False: After the death of his child, David continued to fast and refused to eat bread.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12:20 shows David arose, washed, anointed himself, worshipped, and ate bread after the child died.

questions.question: True or False: David’s servants asked him why he had stopped fasting and weeping after the child’s death, and he explained that he now accepted the child was gone and would go to him.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verses 21-23 record the servants questioning David and his explanation about fasting before the child's death and acceptance after.

questions.question: What does 2 Samuel 12:13-14 teach about God's forgiveness and consequences for sin?
options: God forgives sin but may still bring consequences for it
God never forgives sin once it is committed
There are no consequences if God forgives sin
Sin is always hidden and never exposed
questions.correctAnswer: God forgives sin but may still bring consequences for it
questions.explanation: Verses 13-14 show Nathan telling David that while God put away his sin, the consequences such as the child's death still follow, illustrating forgiveness with consequences.

hard.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 12 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Samuel Chapter 12.

questions.question: What reason does David give for stopping his fasting after the death of his child?
options: He believed the child would come back to life
He acknowledged he could not bring the child back
He was distracted by his enemies
He was told by Nathan to stop fasting
questions.correctAnswer: He acknowledged he could not bring the child back
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12:23 shows David saying he will go to the child but the child will not return, indicating acceptance of death and the futility of fasting.

questions.question: Who was Solomon's other name, and why was he called that?
options: Jedidiah, because of the LORD
Nathaniel, because of the prophet
Jehoshaphat, because of David
Jonathan, because of the people
questions.correctAnswer: Jedidiah, because of the LORD
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12:25 states Nathan the prophet named Solomon 'Jedidiah' meaning 'beloved of the LORD', showing divine favor.

questions.question: What military action did Joab take against Rabbah before David's arrival?
options: He besieged the city but did not enter
He fought and took the royal city
He negotiated a peace treaty
He was defeated and retreated
questions.correctAnswer: He fought and took the royal city
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12:26 records Joab's conquest of Rabbah, capturing the royal city prior to David's direct involvement.

questions.question: What was the weight and material of the king's crown taken from Rabbah's king?
options: A talent of silver with jewels
A talent of gold with precious stones
A heavy bronze crown with engravings
A crown made of iron and gold
questions.correctAnswer: A talent of gold with precious stones
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12:30 describes the crown as weighing a talent of gold and set with precious stones, symbolizing great wealth and authority.

questions.question: What brutal punishments did David impose on the people of Ammon after capturing their cities?
options: They were exiled to another land
They were put under saws, harrows of iron, and axes
They were enslaved and taken to Jerusalem
They were forced to pay tribute and tribute only
questions.correctAnswer: They were put under saws, harrows of iron, and axes
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12:31 records the cruel treatment of captured Ammonites, reflecting ancient Near Eastern wartime practices of total subjugation.

questions.question: How did David show his grief over his sick child before the child's death?
options: He prayed quietly in the temple
He fasted and lay on the ground all night
He held a public mourning ceremony
He sent for the priests to anoint the child
questions.correctAnswer: He fasted and lay on the ground all night
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12:16 reveals David's intense lamentation by fasting and lying on the earth, illustrating a cultural expression of deep mourning.

questions.question: What was the significance of Nathan’s parable about the rich and poor men to David?
options: It was a lesson on generosity to the poor
It was a prophetic indictment of David's sin
It was a story about justice in Israel
It illustrated the blessings of God to kings
questions.correctAnswer: It was a prophetic indictment of David's sin
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12:7 shows Nathan revealing to David that he is the rich man who wronged the poor, exposing David's sin against Uriah.

questions.question: True or False: David immediately confessed his sin after Nathan confronted him.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12:13 records David confessing, 'I have sinned against the LORD,' immediately after Nathan's accusation.

questions.question: True or False: The child born to David and Bathsheba survived and ruled Israel after David.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12:14 and 12:18 indicate the first child of Bathsheba died as a consequence of David's sin, though Solomon, another son, later ruled.

questions.question: What literary device is evident in Nathan's parable involving the rich and poor men, and what is its purpose?
options: Allegory, to symbolize Israel's history
Chiasm, to emphasize the contrast of justice
Parable, to indirectly convict David of his sin
Typology, to foreshadow the Messiah
questions.correctAnswer: Parable, to indirectly convict David of his sin
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12:1-4 uses a parable, a storytelling device, to reveal David's guilt without direct accusation, facilitating self-realization of wrongdoing.

questions.question: What Hebrew word underlies the name 'Jedidiah,' and what does it mean?
options: 'Yedid' meaning 'beloved' or 'friend'
'Jedaiah' meaning 'God is just'
'Jehovah' meaning 'The LORD'
'Sabaoth' meaning 'Hosts or armies'
questions.correctAnswer: 'Yedid' meaning 'beloved' or 'friend'
questions.explanation: The name 'Jedidiah' (2 Samuel 12:25) derives from the Hebrew root 'yedid' meaning 'beloved', signifying God's love for Solomon.

questions.question: Which earlier Old Testament event does David's repentance and forgiveness in this chapter echo?
options: Moses interceding for Israel after the golden calf incident
King Saul's repentance after his disobedience
David's own sin with Goliath
The prophet Jonah's prayer from the fish
questions.correctAnswer: Moses interceding for Israel after the golden calf incident
questions.explanation: David's confession and God's forgiveness (2 Samuel 12:13) parallels Moses' intercession for Israel's sin in Exodus 32, showing divine mercy upon repentance.

questions.question: How does the narrative of David's punishment reflect ancient Near Eastern views of kingship and divine justice?
options: Kings were above divine law and immune to punishment
Kings were symbolic representatives and accountable to God
Kingship guaranteed eternal prosperity regardless of sin
Divine justice was only for common people, not rulers
questions.correctAnswer: Kings were symbolic representatives and accountable to God
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12:10-12 shows David's house suffers consequences for his sin, reflecting that ancient Near Eastern kings were accountable to their deity.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of David's sin and repentance found in this chapter?
options: Romans 4:7-8, David's confession of forgiveness
Revelation 21:4, the new heaven and earth
Matthew 5:3, the Beatitudes
Acts 2:38, repentance and baptism
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 4:7-8, David's confession of forgiveness
questions.explanation: Romans 4:7-8 quotes Psalm 32, attributed to David, reflecting themes of sin acknowledgment and divine forgiveness consistent with 2 Samuel 12:13.

questions.question: What reason does Nathan give for the ongoing sword never departing from David's house?
options: Because David oppressed the poor
Because David took Uriah's wife and despised God
Because David failed to build the temple
Because David did not consult the prophets
questions.correctAnswer: Because David took Uriah's wife and despised God
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12:10 explains the sword will not depart due to David's despising God and taking Uriah's wife, indicating divine judgment on his house.

theological.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 12 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Samuel Chapter 12 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine justice is illustrated by Nathan's parable of the two men, one rich and one poor, in 2 Samuel 12:1-4?
options: God condemns abuse of power and demands restitution for wrongdoing
God values wealth as a sign of righteousness
God ignores the poor and favors the rich
God only punishes the poor for their sins
questions.correctAnswer: God condemns abuse of power and demands restitution for wrongdoing
questions.explanation: Nathan's parable in 2 Samuel 12:1-4 condemns the rich man's exploitation of the poor man's lamb, illustrating that God judges injustice and demands restitution for wrongdoing.

questions.question: What does Nathan's declaration 'Thou art the man' in 2 Samuel 12:7 reveal about God's attribute in confronting sin?
options: God is omniscient and exposes hidden sin
God is indifferent to human actions
God only punishes publicly known sins
God excuses the sins of His anointed
questions.correctAnswer: God is omniscient and exposes hidden sin
questions.explanation: Nathan’s statement in 2 Samuel 12:7 shows that God’s attribute of omniscience enables Him to uncover hidden sin, confronting David directly with his wrongdoing.

questions.question: According to 2 Samuel 12:9-10, what consequence does God declare will never depart from David’s house, and what does this reveal about God's nature?
options: The sword; God’s justice is persistent and consequences are enduring
Blessings; God rewards kings faithfully
Peace; God forgives immediately
Prosperity; God is always merciful
questions.correctAnswer: The sword; God’s justice is persistent and consequences are enduring
questions.explanation: In 2 Samuel 12:9-10, God declares the sword shall never depart from David’s house, revealing that divine justice is persistent and sin has lasting consequences.

questions.question: What theological truth about repentance and forgiveness is taught in 2 Samuel 12:13 when David confesses his sin and Nathan responds?
options: God forgives the repentant sinner and removes the guilt of sin
Confession has no effect on God’s judgment
Forgiveness is automatic without repentance
Sin cannot be forgiven once committed
questions.correctAnswer: God forgives the repentant sinner and removes the guilt of sin
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12:13 teaches that genuine confession leads to God’s forgiveness and removal of guilt, as Nathan tells David the LORD hath put away his sin.

questions.question: What does the death of David’s child in 2 Samuel 12:14-18 signify about the relationship between sin and divine discipline?
options: Sin can bring severe consequences even after forgiveness
God punishes only the sinner, not their household
Discipline is always immediate and public
God never disciplines the children of sinners
questions.correctAnswer: Sin can bring severe consequences even after forgiveness
questions.explanation: Verses 14-18 show that although David’s sin was forgiven, the child’s death illustrates that sin often results in painful consequences as divine discipline.

questions.question: How does David’s response to his child’s death in 2 Samuel 12:20-23 inform our understanding of faith and hope in God amidst suffering?
options: Faith trusts God’s sovereignty and hopes for His grace even in loss
Suffering means God has abandoned His people
Grief should be hidden and faith ignored
God’s grace guarantees no future suffering
questions.correctAnswer: Faith trusts God’s sovereignty and hopes for His grace even in loss
questions.explanation: David’s worship and acceptance in 2 Samuel 12:20-23 demonstrate faith that trusts God’s sovereignty and hopes for grace despite suffering and loss.

questions.question: What does the birth of Solomon in 2 Samuel 12:24-25 reveal about God’s redemptive plan following judgment?
options: God’s mercy restores and continues His covenant promises
Judgment ends God’s relationship with sinners
God rejects all descendants of sinners
Solomon’s birth was unrelated to divine grace
questions.correctAnswer: God’s mercy restores and continues His covenant promises
questions.explanation: The birth of Solomon, loved by the LORD, in 2 Samuel 12:24-25 shows God’s mercy restoring David’s line and continuing His covenantal promises.

questions.question: How does the conquest of Rabbah in 2 Samuel 12:26-31 connect this chapter’s narrative to the broader biblical theme of God’s kingdom establishment?
options: It demonstrates God’s sovereign support for David’s kingship and kingdom expansion
It shows David’s failure as a king
God opposes David’s military actions
The conquest is unrelated to divine purposes
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrates God’s sovereign support for David’s kingship and kingdom expansion
questions.explanation: The victory over Rabbah in 2 Samuel 12:26-31 reflects God’s sovereign support in fulfilling His promise to establish David’s kingdom.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight about sin and divine justice is taught by the verses 2 Samuel 12:5-6 and 2 Samuel 12:11?
options: Sin incurs just punishment and God’s justice will manifest publicly and personally
Sin is ignored if it is secret
God is indifferent to human sin
Punishment is always delayed and hidden
questions.correctAnswer: Sin incurs just punishment and God’s justice will manifest publicly and personally
questions.explanation: Verses 5-6 show David’s judgment of sin deserving death and restitution, while 12:11 declares God will raise evil publicly against David, teaching that sin brings just and public consequences.

questions.question: What does the synthesis of 2 Samuel 12:8 and 2 Samuel 12:13 reveal about the nature of God’s grace towards repentant sinners?
options: God’s grace is abundant and forgiving despite human failure
God withholds blessings after sin
God’s grace depends on human merit
God never forgives kings
questions.correctAnswer: God’s grace is abundant and forgiving despite human failure
questions.explanation: Verse 8 shows God’s generous blessings to David, and verse 13 reveals God’s forgiveness upon repentance, demonstrating abundant grace despite failure.

questions.question: How does the combination of 2 Samuel 12:22-23 and 2 Samuel 12:24-25 inform a Christological understanding of hope beyond death?
options: David’s hope to ‘go to’ his dead child foreshadows the resurrection hope fulfilled in Christ
Death ends all hope and relationship
David denies any afterlife
Solomon’s birth denies resurrection hope
questions.correctAnswer: David’s hope to ‘go to’ his dead child foreshadows the resurrection hope fulfilled in Christ
questions.explanation: David’s statement about going to his child in 12:22-23 anticipates resurrection hope, which is ultimately fulfilled in Christ, as supported by Solomon’s birth in 12:24-25.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that divine punishment described in 2 Samuel 12:31 is cruel and unjust. What does 2 Samuel 12:9-11 actually teach about God's justice and holiness in response to sin?
options: God’s justice is holy and necessary to uphold His moral order against sin
God punishes arbitrarily without cause
God ignores sin and lets evil flourish
God is indifferent to human actions
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice is holy and necessary to uphold His moral order against sin
questions.explanation: Verses 9-11 show that God’s justice is a holy response to sin, necessary to maintain divine moral order, not arbitrary cruelty as sceptics claim.

questions.question: What attribute of God is emphasized by the LORD raising 'evil against thee out of thine own house' in 2 Samuel 12:11?
options: God’s holiness and righteous judgment
God’s indifference
God’s forgetfulness
God’s partiality toward sinners
questions.correctAnswer: God’s holiness and righteous judgment
questions.explanation: The raising of evil within David’s household in 12:11 reflects God’s holiness and righteous judgment against sin.

questions.question: How do 2 Samuel 12:16-17 reveal the sanctification process in response to divine discipline?
options: David’s fasting and humility show sanctification through repentance and submission
Discipline leads to rebellion and hardness
Sanctification ignores God’s discipline
David’s actions show presumption
questions.correctAnswer: David’s fasting and humility show sanctification through repentance and submission
questions.explanation: David’s humble fasting and lying on the earth in 12:16-17 illustrate sanctification as repentance and submission to God’s discipline.

questions.question: What does the narrative arc from David’s sin in 2 Samuel 12:9 to the establishment of Solomon in 12:24-25 teach about God’s redemptive plan?
options: God’s plan includes judgment, repentance, forgiveness, and covenant continuation through a messianic line
God abandons sinners and breaks covenants
Redemption is immediate without consequences
David’s kingdom ends with his sin
questions.correctAnswer: God’s plan includes judgment, repentance, forgiveness, and covenant continuation through a messianic line
questions.explanation: The progression from David’s sin and judgment in 12:9 to Solomon’s birth in 12:24-25 reveals God’s redemptive plan encompassing discipline, repentance, forgiveness, and covenant fulfillment.
